alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 7:21AM MST until November 5 at 11:45PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
...The Flood Watch continues for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa Vicinity/Central San Luis
Valley.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...flooding is forecasted to
begin by mid week.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to Thursday evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached early Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.areaDesc: Alamosa  Vicinity/Central San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 7:19AM MST until November 3 at 7:34PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Moderate Flood. Water flows into farm
properties and homes west of Del Norte. Serious lowland and meadow
flooding occurs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:01 AM MST Monday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:01 AM MST Monday was 6.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.0 feet
late this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.8
feet on 10/05/1911.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 6:14AM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Feet, Upper Rio
Grande Valley and Eastern San Juan Mountains Below 10000 Feet.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location. .

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall Sunday has caused rivers to flood across the
region. High water is expected to occur through the next couple
of days.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the South Fork of the Rio Grande, including South Fork and
Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
alerts.areaDesc: Upper Rio Grande Valley/Eastern San Juan Mountains Below 10000 Ft; Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Ft

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 6:14AM MST until November 4 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be possible,
especially over the western half of San Luis Valley.

* WHERE...The western half of the San Luis Valley, including
Antonito, Del Norte, Monte Vista and Alamosa.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Runoff from heavy rain and melting snow over the San Juan
Mountains may cause flooding in the San Luis Valley, especially
Monday and Tuesday as high flows move out of the mountains and
through the Rio Grande and Conejos River.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte, Monte Vista and Alamosa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
alerts.areaDesc: Del Norte Vicinity/Northern San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Alamosa  Vicinity/Central San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Southern San Luis Valley

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 2 at 3:38AM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations up to 3 to 6
inches. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Feet.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, especially tonight and
Monday morning over Wolf Creek Pass and Cumbres Pass. Strong winds
could produce areas of blowing and drifting snow.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 7:26PM MST until November 2 at 7:30PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
Upstream flooding along the Rio Grande continues downstream near
Monte Vista in Rio Grande County.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Rio Grande near Monte Vista is forecasted
to begin by late morning on Monday.

* WHERE...East Central Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...
West Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...The Rio Grande continues to rise due to upstream flooding
through Del Norte and South Fork. Extensive inundation of low-lying
areas adjacent to the river is expected. Inundation of low spots
along Highway 185, some homes, and other structures may be possible
for areas south of the river. Expect many areas of slow moving or
standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 717 PM MST, Upstream stream gauges on the Rio Grande and South
Fork Rio Grande indicate that flooding is occurring.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Monte Vista.
- http://water.noaa.gov

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:37PM MST until November 2 at 4:30PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the South Fork Rio Grande and mainstem Rio
Grande through South Fork caused by rain and snowmelt is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County in south central Colorado...
West Central Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 430 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the South Fork Rio Grande and mainstem Rio
Grande through South Fork is expected. Additional flooding of
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is
imminent or occurring. Numerous roads remain closed due to
flooding. Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
rainfall and upstream snowmelt.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 433 PM MST, Rain and snowmelt is occurring, and will cause
flooding. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen on top of
melting snow. Stream gauge data indicates that the South Fork Rio
Grande at South Fork will be reaching flood stage soon.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
South Fork and areas along Highway 160 up to Wolf Creek Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Avalanche Advisory issued October 31 at 7:16PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
SABCO

THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE
COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SATURDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...West Elk Mountains, Elk Mountains, San Juan Mountains, and
La Plata Mountains
*WHEN...From 4:30 PM Saturday until 4:30 PM Monday.
*IMPACTS...Backcountry travelers can easily trigger dangerous
avalanches large enough to bury a human.

*PRECAUTION/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...A potent winter storm increases
avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause
natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.

Beyer & Pritchett
